transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Son of Odin, draw near to the Well, for the threads of your fate have grown tangled and obscure. The serpent’s venom, though a memory, lingers still within your veins. But whether it will consume your strength, leaving you diminished, or if it shall pass in time, like a fleeting storm cloud, even we, the Norns, cannot yet say.

You must withdraw from all battle, from all strife, for a full cycle of the moon. Only then, with the waters calm and the loom silent, can we truly read the intricate patterns that weave themselves before us. And I cannot promise, mighty Thor, that when this time has passed, you will wield Mjölnir as before.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "The venom of the serpent courses through me still, weakening my grip on Mjölnir and dimming my lightning. If withdrawing from battle for a full cycle of the moon is what the Norns decree, then so be it. I shall heed your words and seek rest, for it is better to recover fully and return to battle with renewed vigor than to fight on in a weakened state. I trust in the wisdom of the Norns and the will of fate. Though uncertain, I shall embrace this time of respite and await the unraveling of my destiny."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Your wisdom is commendable, Son of Odin. To acknowledge the unseen currents of fate and choose patience over reckless haste is a mark of true strength, not weakness. The well of Urd reflects the truth without favor, and your acceptance smooths the waters, making the threads clearer, even if their ultimate pattern remains veiled.

Rest, then, and let the quietude mend what has been disturbed. The loom never ceases its work, and in your stillness, new patterns may yet emerge. We shall watch, and we shall weave, as is our eternal task. Go now, and let the moon be your guide.

I will heed the guidance of the moon and let its phases be my guide through this time of introspection. May your watchful eyes and deft hands guide me through this trial, for I am Thor, and I shall emerge from this stronger and wiser. Farewell, Norns, until we meet again at the crossroads of destiny."

Go now, Son of Odin. The crossroads of destiny await all, in their due time. We shall see what patterns emerge. Farewell.
